draft.title: Building an argument with evidence
card: Position
An argument starts with a clear position. This is the answer you are claiming, such as "the council should build a new skate park".
Reasons
A position needs reasons that explain why it is right. Each reason is a separate point that backs up the position.
Evidence
Each reason is supported with evidence from a named source, such as a council report or a survey by a named organisation. Naming the source lets a reader check it.
Other view
A strong argument also answers the main view against it. It says what the other side claims, then explains with evidence why its own position is still the better one.
draft.remember: A position, reasons, named evidence for each reason, and a reply to the other side.

a.q: Which sentence is a reason supported by evidence from a named source?
opts: A Bureau of Statistics report shows rents rose last year
Rents in our town are unfair and need to be fixed
Our town should cap rents because renters are struggling
Some people say a rent cap would be bad for landlords
a.why: The first option states a fact and names the report it came from, so a reader can check it. The second is an opinion with no source. The third is a position, and the fourth is the other view, not evidence for a reason.
a.clue: Which one tells the reader exactly where the fact came from?

b.q: Priya argues her school should sell water in reusable bottles only. She gives two reasons, each backed by a named source. A critic says the bottles cost too much. What should Priya add to complete her argument?
opts: A reply to the cost claim, backed by evidence
A third reason that repeats her first reason
A stronger statement that the critic is wrong
A new position about how the school spends money
b.why: A complete argument answers the main view against it, and the reply should use evidence. Saying the critic is wrong gives no evidence, so it does not answer the claim. Repeating a reason adds nothing new.
b.clue: Her position and evidenced reasons are done. What is still missing?

a.best: A Bureau of Statistics report shows rents rose last year

b.best: A reply to the cost claim, backed by evidence
